title: Model G: a phenomenological $\alpha$-cluster binding closure (structural model — not a parameter-free derivation)
html:
Remark. Model G: a phenomenological \alpha-cluster binding closure (structural model — not a parameter-free derivation)

Remark (Model G — a phenomenological closure interpreting the activation gate).

This is a structural/phenomenological model, not a parameter-free derivation. The cluster bindings B(\text{cluster}) enter at their measured AME values (an input); the light-spectator coefficient b = 0.78\ \mathrm{MeV} is calibrated empirically on three one-bond composites; the gated pair coefficient g = 2.4155\ \mathrm{MeV} is a guarded near-match (\approx 3b, -2.9\%); the saturation count \binom{k}{2} is data-selected. Model G derives the composite structure — which \alpha \cdot \alpha pairs activate, via the proved gate prop:alpha-cluster-activation-gate — not the absolute cluster base. It is recorded here for its structural content alone, and must not be cited as an ab-initio prediction.

Applying the activation gate to the light \alpha-conjugate (and \alpha + \text{light-remainder}) isotopes, with cluster decompositions ^6\mathrm{Li} = \alpha + d, ^7\mathrm{Li} = \alpha + t, ^8\mathrm{Be} = 2\alpha, ^9\mathrm{Be} = 2\alpha + n, ^{12}\mathrm{C} = 3\alpha, ^{16}\mathrm{O} = 4\alpha, the model reads

B(\text{isotope}) \;\approx\; \sum_{\text{clusters}} B(\text{cluster})
  \;+\; b\,A_{\text{light}} \;+\; g\,\binom{k}{2}\,[\,k \ge 3\,],

where k is the number of \alpha-clusters, A_{\text{light}} the light-remainder nucleon count, and [\,k\ge 3\,] the Iverson bracket for the gated \alpha\cdot\alpha pair term. The pair term is switched on only for k\ge 3 — the gate's Hopf-spectator closure (part 1 of the proposition) suppresses the k=2 (^8\mathrm{Be}) pair, while a Borromean triple of \alpha-clusters (part 2) opens it.

Residuals (percent of B_{\mathrm{AME}}; ^{12}\mathrm{C} and ^{16}\mathrm{O} are out-of-sample, constants fixed before evaluation):

isotope clusters residual
^6\mathrm{Li} \alpha + d +0.28\%
^7\mathrm{Li} \alpha + t -0.31\%
^8\mathrm{Be} 2\alpha +0.16\%
^9\mathrm{Be} 2\alpha + n -0.02\%
^{12}\mathrm{C} 3\alpha -0.26\%
^{16}\mathrm{O} 4\alpha -0.28\%

Epistemic tiers of the ingredients (the proved gate vs. the fitted closure):

ingredient tier
bond-count multiplicity M_n = n-1 proved-Lean (prop:linear-chain-bond-count)
\bar\mu sign-rep obstruction (coupling through \lvert\bar\mu\rvert only) proved-Lean
Milnor-indeterminacy gate (Hopf spectator \Rightarrow inactive; \alpha-only activation) proved-Lean (+ literature milnor1954)
W-plane annihilation on \mathrm{Vol}=0 bond channels proved-Lean
CAL-3 bond-channel class selection conditional (on the BindingVolumeLedger class)
\alpha\cdot\alpha activation applied to specific isotopes (^8\mathrm{Be}\approx 0, k\ge 3) conditional on the Brunnian arrangement model
b = 0.78\ \mathrm{MeV/nucleon} empirical (calibrated on 3 one-bond composites)
\binom{k}{2} saturation counting data-selected
g = 2.4155 \approx 3b (-2.9\%) guarded near-match
^{11}\mathrm{B} / {}^{14}\mathrm{N} / {}^{19}\mathrm{F} mixed multi-bond open (-58/-33/-10\% deficit)

Numerical verification (checks only; no result elsewhere in this paper depends on them): alpha-activation-brunnian.witness.json (9/9), building on alpha-cluster-volume-additivity.witness.json (7/7) and inter-cluster-bond-term.witness.json (10/10). The ab-initio route for the cluster bases (replacing the AME input) is the separate bond-count tower — ^3\mathrm{H} to \approx 0.16\% with no fit; ^4\mathrm{He} remains open (the \mathrm{Vol}_4 census gap).
